_persona: GOLDEN — plain W-2 wage earner, 2026 epoch year. Expected values were hand-computed from cited primary sources BEFORE the model was run against them; they are not model output. See docs/GOLDEN_CASES.md.
_do_not_repin: These are external anchors, not self-consistency pins. If one of them moves, the model disagrees with the cited source — investigate the model, do not re-pin. scripts/repin_personas.py must always report 0 moved here.

_sources.rp_25_32: IRS Rev. Proc. 2025-32 — 2026 single brackets (10% to 12,400 / 12% to 50,400 / 22% to 105,700 / 24% to 201,775 / 32% to 256,225 / 35% to 640,600 / 37% above) and standard deduction $16,100. https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-drop/rp-25-32.pdf
_sources.ssa_2025_10_24: SSA announcement 2025-10-24 — 2026 Social Security wage base $184,500; max employee SS tax $11,439 (6.2%).
_sources.irc_3101b2: IRC §3101(b)(2) — Additional Medicare Tax 0.9% on wages over $200,000 (single). Statutory, unindexed.

_excluded: CA bracket-derived fields (ca_taxable, ca_income_tax, total_tax, take_home, effective_tax_rate) carry no golden claim — the 2026 CA tables are still projected from 2025 actuals.

w2_200k._source: base_salary 200,000; everything else zeroed. Wages sit exactly ON the $200,000 Additional Medicare threshold.

2026._fica_social_security: min(200,000, 184,500) x 6.2% = 11,439.00 [ssa_2025_10_24] — the published max employee SS tax
2026._fica_additional_medicare: max(0, 200,000 - 200,000) x 0.9% = 0.00 [irc_3101b2] — AT the threshold, not over it

w2_300k._source: base_salary 300,000; everything else zeroed. Above both the SS wage base and the Additional Medicare threshold.

w2_pretax_max._source: base_salary 200,000 with a 20%-of-base pre-tax election (desired 40,000) — the §402(g) limit binds.

2026._gross_income: wages only: 200,000 (the deferral is withheld from, not subtracted before, gross)
2026._fica_social_security: elective deferrals are FICA wages: min(200,000, 184,500) x 6.2% = 11,439.00 [ssa_2025_10_24] — unchanged by the deferral
2026._fica_medicare: 200,000 x 1.45% = 2,900.00 — also unchanged by the deferral
